record.original_question: A graph is called orientably simple if it embeds in the torus T but not in the Klein bottle K. Characterize the orientably simple graphs, without assuming that the characterization must be by excluded minors.

evidence.quote: A graph G that embeds in T but not K we call orientably simple. The problem is to characterize orientably simple graphs, not necessarily by excluded minors.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T$ denote the torus (the closed orientable surface of genus 1) and let $K$ denote the Klein bottle (the closed nonorientable surface of nonorientable genus 2). A finite graph $G$ is said to be orientably simple if $G$ admits a topological embedding into $T$ but does not admit any topological embedding into $K$.

Give a structural characterization of the class of orientably simple graphs. The characterization is not required to be in terms of excluded minors; any intrinsic structural description (for example, in terms of constructions, decompositions, embedding schemes, or other graph-theoretic invariants) is acceptable.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return a definitive characterization of graphs that embed in the torus but not in the Klein bottle. Related work addresses spanning planar subgraphs, vertex-transitive graphs, and colorings on these surfaces, and there is research on the (large) family of forbidden minors for the torus, but no general structural characterization of orientably simple graphs appears to be established. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Spanning Planar Subgraphs of Graphs in the Torus and Klein Bottle
status_evidence.snippet: Every 3-connected graph embedded in the torus or the Klein bottle has a spanning planar subgraph...
status_evidence.claim: Related structural results exist for graphs in the torus and Klein bottle, but they do not characterize graphs embedding in T but not in K.

status_evidence.title: Tilings of the torus and the Klein bottle and vertex-transitive graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Regular tilings of the torus and Klein bottle, with applications to vertex-transitive graphs on these surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature on torus/Klein bottle embeddings does not provide a known characterization of orientably simple graphs.
